edge.title: The government deadline that arrives with a link
edge.setup: Ration card e-KYC is due soon. A message or a helpful stranger says it must be done today, shares a link or app, and mentions a small 'processing fee' or asks for an OTP to 'complete verification'.
edge.tell: A real deadline, delivered through a channel you did not open yourself, asking for money or an OTP.
move: Do not tap the link or share any OTP. Go to the department's own website or office, which you reach yourself.
Check the deadline on the official notice, not in the message that is pushing you.
If you already shared an OTP or paid, call your bank and the 1930 cybercrime helpline now.
edge.why: Scammers do not need to invent urgency when a real deadline already exists. They ride on it. The deadline is true; the channel is the fake. So judge who contacted whom, not whether the deadline is real.
edge.variants: Same shape: PAN-Aadhaar linking 'last date' texts, FASTag KYC calls, electricity 'disconnection tonight' messages, bank KYC-update links.

lens.name: Planning fallacy
lens.one_line: We estimate time and cost from the best-case plan, so projects almost always run late and over budget.
lens.detail: People picture the plan going smoothly and forget the delays that hit every real project: approvals, weather, supply, rework. Asking 'how long did similar projects actually take?' gives a far better estimate than asking 'how long should this take?'. It is the base rate applied to schedules.
elsewhere: Home renovations finishing weeks after the contractor's date.
Your own 'it will take ten minutes' tasks.
lens.test: What did the last three similar things actually take, and why would this one be different?
lens.today: Realty Today reports North Bengaluru's Metro-led property push is selling connectivity before it is complete, and Deccan Herald says the Pink Line's underground stretch has reached ₹1,000 crore per km a decade on. Both stories rest on a completion date that was best-case when announced. If you are paying more for a flat because a station is 'coming soon', price it as if the line opens years later than the brochure says.
